evaluation: JD prompt legacy/XML A/B with safeguard telemetry

executionProtocol.requiredOrder: legacy process exits successfully before XML process starts
executionProtocol.reason: DeepSeek provider concurrency limits make parallel A/B execution invalid.

historicalContext: The instrumented repeat is a pre-fix bounded reparse gate run; its values and case details are retained as historical evidence and are not new live results.

captures: low-level response body read errors and timeout attempts
critic JSON validity and issue object schema completeness
first review versus second review provider attempts
normalized safeguard verdict, issue severity, reparse status, and scorer output

xml.source: working tree XML based on HEAD d04ca51

delta.interpretation: The repeat has no positive score direction and has more reparses, timeouts, and incomplete critic issue schemas in the XML variant.

findings.finding: The pre-fix XML instrumented repeat produced valid JSON objects with a valid revise verdict, but the critic issue objects were incomplete.
findings.evidence: All 10 non-timeout XML critic responses in the instrumented repeat had issue objects with field and severity but no problem or action; the telemetry classified all 10 as invalid issue schema.

findings.finding: The pre-fix gate, at the time of the instrumented repeat, treated every first-attempt revise verdict as reparse-eligible when an attempt remained.
findings.evidence: The pre-fix backend/src/services/jobDescription/jdParseGateService.js returned shouldReparse=true for revise without checking that issue details were complete or that a high-severity issue was grounded.

findings.finding: Pre-fix normalization hid incomplete issue details instead of preserving the provider-schema failure.
findings.evidence: The pre-fix backend/src/services/agenticSafeguards/safeguardShared.js filled missing problem with Unspecified safeguard issue. and missing action with an empty string.

findings.finding: XML improves JD extraction or reduces hallucination in general.
findings.evidence: The initial pair was +0.5 percentage points, while the instrumented repeat was -0.4 percentage points and critical average fell from 1.000 to 0.992. The scorer does not directly measure hallucination rate.

limitations: Only six fixtures were used in each run.
The two variants were run sequentially against a live provider; timeout and response variability are visible confounders.
No human-labeled ground truth was added for whether each critic issue was a true positive or false positive.
The runner records telemetry summaries only; raw prompts and provider responses are not persisted.
